metadata.description: Master cross-paradigm evaluation and comparative audit for CM3604 Phase 8.

model_comparison_records.name: Random Guess (seed=42)
model_comparison_records.primary_strength: Zero parameter overhead; provides uninformative stochastic lower bound.
model_comparison_records.primary_vulnerability: Completely blind to semantic evidence and fact content.

model_comparison_records.name: Always Supported
model_comparison_records.primary_strength: Maximizes Supported recall (100.0%); trivial zero-rule baseline without evaluating passages.
model_comparison_records.primary_vulnerability: Total failure on Not Supported class (0.0% precision, recall, F1); blind to evidence.

model_comparison_records.name: Task 1: Word Overlap (P4 Porter-Stemmed)
model_comparison_records.primary_strength: Fast CPU inference; strong surface lexical recall and numerical entity alignment.
model_comparison_records.primary_vulnerability: Lexical overlap deceived by topic words (16 FPs); lacks semantic negation awareness.

model_comparison_records.name: Task 2: DeBERTa-v3 Entailment
model_comparison_records.primary_strength: Deep semantic reasoning; high NS recall (92.66%), NS precision (78.91%), and low false positives (8 FPs).
model_comparison_records.primary_vulnerability: Higher computational latency (CPU); false negatives on multi-hop/numeric claims (27 FNs).

comparative_error_analysis.oracle_union_diagnostic_note: Theoretical diagnostic upper bound assuming an oracle selector choosing the correct prediction if either model is correct; not a trained hybrid model.
comparative_error_analysis.synthesis_insight: Task 1 (Word Overlap) and Task 2 (DeBERTa-v3) exhibit complementary error profiles: Task 2 achieves exceptional sensitivity on Not Supported claims (92.66% NS recall, 78.91% NS precision, only 8 FPs vs Task 1's 16 FPs), successfully rejecting lexical distractors. Conversely, Task 1 maintains higher recall on multi-hop and numeric Supported claims (17 FNs vs Task 2's 27 FNs). Only 15 facts represent common failures across both paradigms, and an oracle union yields 93.21% accuracy as a diagnostic theoretical upper bound (not a trained hybrid model), highlighting strong potential for hybrid lexical-neural fact-checking architectures.
